question: In Britain, almost every household appliance carries its own small fuse, tucked inside a part you hold every time you connect it to the wall. Which part?
source_excerpt: BS 1363 plugs are required to carry a BS 1362 cartridge fuse.

extra.why_interesting: Most players think of fuses or breakers as living in a box in the hallway. They'll be surprised that in Britain every appliance has its own fuse in an object they handle daily. The stem's clue lets them reason their way to it.
extra.verification_notes: BS 1363 plugs in the UK contain a BS 1362 cartridge fuse, so 'the plug' is correct; no newer developments contradict this (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BS_1363).

explanation: British homes often wire sockets on one big ring circuit protected for high current, so a fuse inside each plug protects the thin cable of your lamp or kettle. If that fuse blows, you just unscrew the plug and swap it.
